subject: [PATCH v1] mm/memcontrol: drop non-hierarchical memcg-wide stats in non-v1 kernels

reviews.author: Yosry Ahmed
reviews.summary: Reviewer Yosry Ahmed suggested querying the boot parameter instead of relying on the CONFIG_MEMCG_V1 configuration option, as it would still be possible to disable v1 even if it's not explicitly set in the kernel configuration.
reviews.raw_body:
Can we query the boot parameter instead of the config option here?
IIUC this should work even if v1 is only disabled at boot.

reviews.author: Joanne Koong (author)
reviews.summary: Author agrees that gating the non-hierarchical stats behind cgroup_subsys_on_dfl() is a good idea, suggesting it as an additional step to cover CONFIG_MEMCG_V1=y kernels not using v1. They propose populating state_local and events_local arrays from aggregated state/events arrays in a .bind callback.
reviews.raw_body:
This seems like a good idea to me. Maybe we should take it one step
further and gate it behind cgroup_subsys_on_dfl() to cover any
CONFIG_MEMCG_V1=y kernel that doesn't use/mount v1? Not a memcg expert
but afaict, if the kernel then switches from default (v2) to legacy
(v1), we could populate the state_local and events_local arrays from
the aggregated state / events arrays in a .bind callback since
switching from v2 to v1 is only allowed if there's no memcg subtrees.

Thanks,
Joanne

2026-09-01.patch_summary: This patch optimizes the Linux kernel's memory control group (memcg) statistics by dropping non-hierarchical memcg-wide stats in kernels that don't support version 1 of memcg. This is done by compiling out the non-hierarchical arrays when CONFIG_MEMCG_V1=n, which reduces the number of cachelines pulled in during flush operations and makes them cheaper. The patch also includes benchmark results showing a 2-4% reduction in flush time on an 80-cpu x86_64 machine with 500 cgroups. The changes do not affect kernel builds with CONFIG_MEMCG_V1=y, which continue to support the legacy memory.stat and memory.numa_stat readers.
